bull.b: Royal Caribbean shows a durable profitability recovery: high TTM margins and scaled revenue underpin sustainable earnings generation. Strong margins reflect pricing power and cost efficiencies that support reinvestment, debt servicing and shareholder returns across travel cycles.

Consistent operating cash flow ($6.8B TTM) and sizable liquidity provide durable funding for capex, ship orders and capital returns. Strong cash generation enabled refinancing actions and buybacks, reducing rollover risk and supporting strategic investments over the medium term.

Ongoing fleet modernization, new destination development and digital/loyalty initiatives strengthen differentiation and repeat demand. Higher digital penetration and pre-cruise upsell embed guests in the ecosystem, raising lifetime value and resilient ancillary revenue streams.

bear.b: Material leverage leaves the company more exposed to demand shocks and higher interest rates. Even after improvement, leverage constrains strategic flexibility, amplifies refinancing and interest-cost risk, and makes sustained investment or payout growth contingent on dependable cash conversion.

Negative TTM free cash flow despite strong accounting profits signals that investment, working-capital swings or timing effects are outpacing cash generation. With elevated debt, inconsistent FCF limits sustainable deleveraging and curbs the durability of buybacks/dividends during cyclical downturns.

Fuel-price exposure remains a recurring margin risk despite hedges, and regulatory setbacks (permit denial for Perfect Day Mexico) can materially delay or raise the cost of high-return expansion projects. Combined, these factors can compress returns and postpone strategic growth benefits.
